svg.text: Three trees, one process today · modular monolith behind a JSON API · dependency always pointing inward · boundaries checked by tooling, not by agreement
Artefact 1 — apps/web : the React SPA. It holds no rule; it asks, shows and sends.
app/ — the shell and the routes
React Router decides the URL; the guard decides
the area by role. Every area ends with a catch-all,
so a typo is a screen and not a blank page.
a guardian never downloads the registrar screens.
It mints the Idempotency-Key, sets X-Requested-By
and turns an error body into a message. Nowhere
else in the front does fetch get called.
JSON over a first-party session cookie, refreshed on every load.
Artefact 3 — packages/contracts : the only tree both halves import
13 files of types and four frozen enumerations, with zero imports of their own —
so this arrow can never drag the server graph into the browser bundle.
The first import is config: it validates the environment and throws. A process that starts without DATABASE_URL finds out in the middle of an enrollment.
Bun.serve({ fetch: app.fetch }) · startScheduler([sessionPurge]) — the only point outside http/ that calls a module directly
SIGTERM/SIGINT: stop accepting → drain what is in flight → let the jobs finish → close the pool. In that order, so the queue does not grow while draining.
Interface (delivery) — apps/api/src/http/ : HTTP in, JSON out, plus the front's build served beside it. No business rule lives here.
Hono. The chain order is the semantics:
onError repeats the error middleware because
Hono will not let the exception reach next().
Health, then the API, then static — last.
announcements. schemas/ holds the Zod of every
/assets/<name with the hash> is immutable; every
other path is index.html, which is never cached.
A path the server owns and does not have is a 404,
never the document. secureWrite refuses a write
that did not come from the application itself.
Modules — four bounded contexts in the same process. Each has its domain, its application and its infra; none sees inside another.
who signs in, with what role
zod validates at the edge; what
zod validates at the edge; what
zod validates at the edge; what
zod validates at the edge; what
Shared kernel — apps/api/src/shared/ : infrastructure with no business rule. The arrow never goes from here up into a module.
where the S04 Mailer will fit
CPF is a pure value: the same
a limit keeps a single owner
infrastructure — open to application/ and infra/, closed to the domain
zod at boot; a missing variable
slice() and typed page, used by
PostgreSQL — 18 tables, 16 of them scoped by network_id
identity: network, school, app_user, user_role, session · academics: academic_year, subject, class_group,
class_group_subject, student, student_guardian, enrollment · assessment: grade, attendance, term_closing
communication: announcement, announcement_recipient · platform: idempotent_request (no network_id)
Vite hashes every bundle; index.html names them.
The name carries the content, so a one-year
application/ and infra/ use everything here
Bun.sql · the transaction is opened in one place only
One process serves all three trees today
I23: three variables move the front to a CDN with no code
change — as long as it stays a subdomain of the same site.
What crosses the boundary is types, and only types. The API
and the SPA both import packages/contracts; neither imports
identity is the leaf: it knows nobody — and that is why the
other three are allowed to point at it. assessment is allowed
to reach it too and does not: it gets there through academics.
Every arrow crosses through index.ts. domain/, application/
The rules `bun run check` rejects — three cruises, one per tree
A module only sees another through index.ts. When billing/ is extracted at
S14, the list of dependents is exactly whoever imports the index.
The domain does not know a database, HTTP, a log, a scheduler or a
third-party library exists. It reaches ports/, result.ts, document/ and constants.
A use case may name exactly one third-party package: zod. Anything else is
an effect, and an effect belongs behind a port — which is where S04's Mailer goes.
shared/ imports no context at all. That is why shared/http/session.ts declares
the shape of the user instead of importing it from identity.
apps/web — source and suite alike — may import packages/contracts and nothing
else from this repository. Written as a permission, so nothing slips through unnamed.
Nothing outside packages/contracts/src may be imported from inside it. A
contract is shape, and shape has no dependencies.
Decisions the blueprint does not show on its own
unitOfWork() is the application's only commit point. The Idempotency-Key claim is its
first statement, and a refusal returned from inside it rolls the transaction back.
reader(), readerFresh() and writer() are three names over one pool. I15 declares which
of them the replica may never answer; switching at S08 touches no repository.
The key comes from the application
uuidIdGenerator produces the UUID: parent and child in the same transaction, with no
round trip to learn the parent's id.
pg_advisory_xact_lock on (class group, term) is what stops closing a term and posting
into it from interleaving. It is released by the commit, not by code.
bun run verify = typecheck → check (depcruise) → magic (literals with no owner) →
test → budget (the browser bundle). None of the five is optional.
solid arrow — a real import, checked at compile time
dashed arrow — application/ calls the repositories in infra/
arrow rejected by depcruise: the build breaks if anyone tries
The colours say the layer, not the module:
facade — the bounded context's only door
application — orchestrates, validates, opens the transaction
domain — thick border: the core, framework-free
ports — what the domain is allowed to know
The blueprint is Stage 01's. It was already drawn with S14 in mind.
Read from apps/api/src/, apps/web/src/, packages/contracts/src/ and the three .dependency-cruiser.js. State of Stage 01.
